_comment: Expansion 6: what the politics engine says of threats (world/threats.py): a beast brought down by a hero of the history, a dead king laid to rest by others, a place emptied by a doom, a place filling again, a gang grown bold, a beast killed in a lord's great hunt, an outlaw's band broken by a lord's riders (G.2).

threat_hunted: {hero} brought {beast} down at last, in its lair at {home}, and came home with its head.
The hunt is over: {hero} killed {beast} in {home}. The farms round about lit fires all night.
{beast} is dead. {hero} tracked it to {home} and finished it there, and will not say what it cost.
Word from {home}: {hero} has slain {beast}, that the shepherds feared for a lifetime.
threat_emptied: {place} is empty. Those who lived went in the night, and {villain} has the fields.
The last families have left {place}. Nobody would stay another winter with {villain} so near.
{place} stands empty: doors open, hearths cold. The people who are left say {villain} drove them out.
No smoke over {place} now. {villain} took too many, and the rest took to the roads.
threat_rebuilding: Smoke over {place} again: families have come back to mend the roofs and sow the fields.
Settlers are coming to {place}, some of them its own folk, some strangers, all of them hopeful.
{place} is filling again. The first harvest since the bad years is in, and the inn has opened its shutters.
The empty houses of {place} have people in them again: a smith's fire, washing on the lines, children in the lane.
threat_laid: The priests of {place} went up to {home} with bell and candle, and {villain} lies still again. The dead have stopped walking.
{villain} is at rest. Pilgrims from {place} sealed {home} with prayers and stone, and the nights in {area} are quiet.
A hermit went into {home} alone, and came out at dawn grey-haired. Since then the dead of {villain} have not been seen.
Word from {area}: {home} is shut again. Whoever woke {villain} could not keep him awake, and the dogs of {place} have stopped howling.
threat_gang_grows: {gang} has doubled its numbers: deserters, runaways and worse have gone up to {home} to ride with {villain}.
{villain}'s men rode through {area} forty strong. {gang} is no longer a band of robbers but a little army.
Recruits keep coming to {gang} at {home}. {villain} pays in silver taken off the roads.
There are more of {gang} every week. {villain} turns nobody away who can hold a blade.
threat_great_hunt: {lord} called a great hunt on {villain}: hounds and beaters went up to {home}, and its head hangs on a gate now.
{villain} is dead. The huntsmen of {lord} ran it down near {home} with a hundred spears, and lost good men doing it.
Word from {area}: the great hunt of {lord} found {villain} at {home} and finished it. The farms of {place} feast tonight.
The horns of {lord} were heard over {area} for three days. On the fourth, they brought {villain} down below {home}.
threat_broken: The riders of {lord} burned {gang} out of {home}. {villain} was hanged at the crossroads above {place}.
{gang} is finished: {lord} sent soldiers to {home}, and {villain} swung for it before the week was out.
Word from {area}: {lord}'s men took {home} by night, and the roads round {place} are free of {gang}.
{villain} is dead on a rope, and {gang} scattered to the hills. {lord} has had enough of tolls on its roads.
